Correlation matrix plot

Source: R/empirical_plot.R
plot_cors.Rd

Heatmap version of correlation matrix to visualize bivariate correlations.

Usage

plot_cors(
  r,
  numbers = TRUE,
  colors = TRUE,
  n = 51,
  main = NULL,
  zlim = c(-1, 1),
  show.legend = TRUE,
  labels = NULL,
  select = NULL,
  pval = NULL,
  cuts = c(0.001, 0.01),
  stars = FALSE,
  pdigits = 3,
  scale = TRUE,
  cex = 1,
  thresh = 0.2,
  min.cex = 0.6,
  drop.zero = TRUE,
  fit = TRUE,
  fill = 0.9,
  upper = TRUE,
  diag = TRUE,
  symmetric = TRUE,
  xaxis = 1,
  xlas = 90,
  gr = NULL,
  digits = 2,
  alpha = 0.75,
  border = "white",
  ...
)

Arguments

r

square matrix (correlations, or any matrix with values on a common scale), or a data.frame/non-square matrix of raw data, in which case cor(r, use = "pairwise.complete.obs") is computed

numbers

print the (rounded) values in the cells

colors

if FALSE, a grey scale is used

n

number of colour bins

main

title

zlim

range of the colour scale (values are clamped to it)

show.legend

draw the colour key

labels

variable names (default: dimnames of r)

select

indices/names of the variables to show

pval

optional matrix of p-values (same dim as r). If supplied, the upper triangle shows the p-values as plain text with no colour fill, and the lower triangle/diagonal show the coloured correlations

cuts

p-value cutpoints for stars, e.g. c(.001, .01) -> *** / ** / * (a final single * is used for p < .05)

stars

optionally draw significance stars after the lower-triangle correlations (requires pval; FALSE by default, since the p-values themselves are shown in the upper triangle)

pdigits

decimals for printed p-values (smaller values print as <.001)

scale

if TRUE, text is drawn at size cex for every cell (diagonal included) whose |r| >= thresh, and shrinks linearly with |r| below thresh

cex

A common shrink factor is set from the bulk of the labels (not the single widest one), then any label that still overflows its own cell is capped individually

thresh

|r| below which the text starts to shrink

min.cex

smallest relative text size (reached as |r| -> 0)

drop.zero

drop the leading zero of the printed values (.45, -.45)

fit

if TRUE, text is shrunk (never enlarged) to fit the drawn cells; the size is measured at draw time, so it adapts to the device.

fill

proportion of a cell width/height the typical label may fill

upper

draw the upper triangle?

diag

draw the diagonal?

symmetric

if TRUE and r is square, row i is plotted in the same position as column i

xaxis

1 = x labels at the bottom, 3 = at the top

xlas

rotation (degrees) of x labels

gr

colour-ramp function, e.g., colorRampPalette(c("red","white","blue"))

digits

digits shown in cells

alpha

transparency of the cell colours

border

colour of cell borders (NA/"transparent" for none)

...

passed on to lattice::levelplot()
